scientific_integrity: The proof explicitly uses Aliabadi's published cycle-tiling and subgroup-support theorems, proves the new two-involution dihedral base case for arbitrary \(n\), and then derives the ambient divisibility criterion. Prior \(n=3\) and \(n=4\) cases are identified as prior work rather than claimed as new.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns only multisets supported on two distinct involutions \(s,t\) with \(\operatorname{ord}(st)\ge3\). It does not classify arbitrary quotient-realizable multisets in dihedral groups or settle all of Problem 7.7. Finite enumeration is a stress-test only; the infinite family is proved symbolically.
title: A divisibility criterion for two-involution quotient multisets
